title: Award Seat FOMO Thermometer
oneLiner: A playful travel points timing game that turns award-seat screenshots, cash fares, and family date pressure into a book-now-or-wait card.
targetUser: Points travelers planning fixed-date family trips, friend trips, or event travel while comparing paid award tools and cash fares.
keyUX: Enter points cost, fees, cash fare, dates, flexibility, and airline reliability; watch the FOMO thermometer move; then generate a shareable verdict for the group chat.
sourceSignals: S11 - Reddit r/awardtravel June 2026 weekly help thread: https://www.reddit.com/r/awardtravel/comments/1ttnjbl/weekly_help_thread_june_01_2026/
S12 - DOT June 2026 Air Travel Consumer Report: https://www.transportation.gov/resources/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/june-2026-air-travel-consumer-report-april-2026
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app called "Award Seat FOMO Thermometer" for points travelers planning fixed-date family trips, friend trips, or event travel while comparing paid award tools and cash fares. The app is based on observed user pull: travelers already check paid award-seat tools, ask weekly community threads to sanity-check redemptions, compare cash fares, and worry about airline reliability before committing points. The app should use a playful thermometer mechanic around the trigger moment "an award seat appears for fixed dates and the family group chat wants an answer" and make the first screen communicate "Is this seat a win or just panic?" Use the user's own language: "I need to prove this is a smart redemption before the seat disappears." Build the core workflow around points cost, taxes/fees, current cash fare, date flexibility, traveler count, airline risk, paid-tool screenshot, and group-chat pressure, and produce a book-now/wait verdict card. Required sections: trip pressure header, points vs cash input cards, seat scarcity and date-lock thermometer, airline reliability/risk strip, family blame meter, book-now/wait decision dial, screenshot evidence tray, and shareable verdict card. Emotional pressure to make visible: 외로움, family blame, points regret, and fear of missing the trip. Design direction: use the `playful-experimental` profile with a polished travel-game composition, bold boarding-pass cards, one vivid teal/orange heat scale, charming but readable verdict stickers, stable mobile layout, and no generic travel dashboard. Avoid generic dashboard framing; make the main interaction feel like a screenshot-worthy FOMO meter that turns a messy points decision into a group-chat card.
